ResearchProjectDef.label: underwater survival
ResearchProjectDef.description: Drilling rigs to bore through the ice sea, and the basic techniques and life support that let colonists work and survive underwater.\n\nUnlocks the ice shaft, diving suit, watertight door and bilge pump.

ResearchProjectDef.label: pressure engineering
ResearchProjectDef.description: Thick-walled structures that can hold back the water pressure below the thermocline, and pressure-rated decks laid over open water. Ordinary walls are slowly crushed at that depth; going further down means switching to a pressure-rated hull.\n\nUnlocks the pressure hull wall and the hull platform.

ResearchProjectDef.label: submarine construction
ResearchProjectDef.description: Assembling pressure compartments into a submarine that can sail on its own. Once built, it can leave the ice shaft behind and travel to other parts of the ocean.\n\nUnlocks the keel frames, the submarine helm and the underwater thruster.

ResearchProjectDef.label: abyssal navigation
ResearchProjectDef.description: The limits of what a hull and a crew can endure in the deep: magnetohydrodynamic propulsion that is almost silent, hard suits for leaving the hull at depth, and the pressurisation procedures needed before stepping out into the abyss.\n\nUnlocks the advanced underwater thruster.

ResearchProjectDef.label: underwater combat
ResearchProjectDef.description: Finding and fighting other vessels in the dark: sonar arrays that hear across the ocean, and the tactics of hiding behind the thermocline.\n\nUnlocks the active sonar, the passive sonar, the torpedo tube and torpedoes.
